text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.6% today to close at $395.61, marking the third losing day in a row after peaking at $414.65 on November 13th. The stock's weakness comes as oil prices have drifted lower (U.S. crude at $89.62/barrel, down from recent highs), which pressures refiner margins—the spread between what refiners pay for crude and what they can sell refined products for. While refineries are running near capacity at 95.2%, the decline in oil prices and broader inventory levels (gasoline and diesel storage both elevated) suggest softer near-term demand or pricing pressure on refined fuels.

The two-week decline of 7.4% reflects a pullback from earlier optimism, even as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East linger (Iran's escalating rhetoric and attacks in the Gulf). Those tensions haven't sustained crude prices at higher levels, and without the tailwind of rising oil costs, Marathon—as a refiner dependent on healthy margins—loses one of its key profit drivers.
